provenFindings.finding: Continuous actual-app hardware run reproduced the delay with frequent successful poll scheduling, so the historical SwiftShader polling-starvation lesson does not explain this run.
Holding RAF until the first fence signals retained a multi-second gap with exactly one original full-scene render. Later application frames are not necessary for the delay.

Detailed trace locates the long operation on CrGpuMain in TraceGLAPI::glFenceSync. GPU-process CPU time rises substantially during that interval; this is not evidence of five seconds of JavaScript or pure device GPU execution.

Omitting the probe fence did not eliminate the native stall: it moved to SharedImageStub::OnDestroySharedImage -> GLContextEGL::MakeCurrent -> TraceEGLAPI::eglMakeCurrent. The probe can change where submission work occurs; removing it does not prove a startup speedup.
A trusted native Shift-plus event and camera HUD response completed while the first fence remained pending.
